1.reproduce_code:
import React from 'react';
import { RadioButton, RadioButtonGroup } from 'carbon-components-react';

function App() {
  return (
    <RadioButtonGroup
      legendText="Radio Button heading"
      name="radio-button-group"
      defaultSelected="default-selected"
    >
      <RadioButton
        labelText="Radio button label"
        value="standard"
        id="radio-1"
        aria-label="Radio button label" // This is the problematic line
      />
      <RadioButton
        labelText="Radio button label"
        value="default-selected"
        id="radio-2"
      />
      <RadioButton
        labelText="Radio button label"
        value="disabled"
        id="radio-3"
        disabled
      />
    </RadioButtonGroup>
  );
}

export default App;
1.explanation: The code provided sets up a simple React application using the Carbon Design System's RadioButton and RadioButtonGroup components. The issue is reproduced by including an `aria-label` attribute on the first RadioButton, which is unnecessary and causes the screen reader to fail to read the label. Removing this attribute should resolve the issue.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario involves a screen reader not being able to read the label of a radio button in a React component using the Carbon Design System. The issue is that the React version of the radio button includes an unnecessary `aria-label` attribute, which seems to interfere with the screen reader's ability to read the label. In contrast, the vanilla HTML version does not have this issue and the screen reader reads the label correctly.
